Ever since I switched to mainly drinking loose leaf tea, I've found it difficult to drink generic brands that come in tea bags. Most of the "tea" isn't even real tea (Camellia sinensis,) they're just herbal blends. When I do drink with a bag, it's when I'm away from the house or I'm bagging it myself.

Overall, nothing really compares to loose leaf, some teas even need the extra space to open their leaves and release their flavor. There's simply no way you could get the full flavor out of an oolong or puh-er using a bag.

Thoughts?

Agree 100%, if it's in a bag I ain't drinkin' it.

Okay, sometimes when I need the convenience I do. Like for camping or something. Or if it's the only thing around.
Convenience is the word for it. I won't do it if I have the option, usually. Some blends I have are too fine for my strainer so I'll put it in a bag. Other than that, loose leaf is the way to go.
Loose leaf is the way to go

Both have their strengths. Loose leaf has better taste profile but can vary between batches, especially if you live in a part of the world where it takes a long time to get tea shipped to you. What bagged teas have though is consistency. Throw two bags into a cup, brew it for the same time, add same amount of sugar and milk and you'll always have the same taste profile. Some teas aren't really suitable for bagged stuff though, so you should experiment with that as well.

But yes, since oolong and pu-er require special care and very special tea leaves, I'd say it's impossible to create a good consistent bagged version of those. Besides, considering the fact that both these teas are really not something you causally drink (at least that's how it is for me) it's kind of blasphemic to want to even try those in bagged form.

But, I'll say this: NOTHING beats a good cup of PG tips in the morning, I've yet to find a loose leaf that can match the consistency and taste profile of that.

Edit: Also, has anyone here ever used a yixing teapot? I've been thinking about getting into oolong again and if there's any science behind the claims about those pots, I think it's worth buying one now so I can get a good taste in a few years time.
